system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
The Seller’s “[STANDARD]” labels and efficiency note do **not** establish Buyer agreement. All positions remain subject to review. The recommendations below assume the agreed **AUD 24 million, debt-free/cash-free acquisition under NSW law**; proposed negotiating targets are not existing agreed terms.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation — one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A higher, commercially meaningful general cap, with separate treatment of protected categories. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, subject to diligence and recovery security; 20% leaves substantial acquisition risk with Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only the excess. | Lower thresholds, related claims aggregated, and a tipping basket recovering qualifying claims from the first dollar once triggered. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, excluding protected categories; the proposed combination materially erodes recovery. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | Notice within **18 months**, with limitations extended to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | **24–36 months** for general warranties, workable notice requirements and separate category-specific periods. | **Seek 36 months**, preserving timely notified claims until resolved; 18 months may not expose issues across sufficient reporting cycles. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to general caps and time limits. | Separate fundamental warranties covering capacity, ownership, all issued shares and freedom from encumbrances; no basket/de minimis, longer survival and at least purchase-price recovery. | **Reject general treatment; seek a 100% price cap and substantially longer survival**, with fraud separately uncapped; defective title threatens the entire investment. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | No express fraud carve-out is supplied; limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance purport to cover all Claims. | Express protection for fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation, including relevant Seller representatives, and preservation of non-excludable rights. | **Carve fraud out of all caps, thresholds, time bars, disclosure, knowledge and remedy restrictions**; boilerplate must not purport to shelter fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, referenced material, Accounts, registers and public records. | Only sufficiently detailed, fair disclosure against identified warranties, using an agreed, frozen and accessible disclosure record. | **Reject blanket/deemed disclosure and require specific, intelligible disclosures**; document availability alone does not explain a risk’s nature and scope. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Any Buyer/adviser knowledge, including matters merely discoverable from the data room or public records, bars claims. | Prefer no knowledge exclusion; fallback limited to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer individuals, without imputation or enquiry duties. | **Delete constructive/discoverable knowledge and adviser-wide attribution**, expressly preserving indemnities; the draft transfers diligence risk wholesale to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied by delivery of written consent, although no final consent or satisfaction evidence is supplied. | A Buyer-benefit completion condition requiring valid consent **and satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions**, without unacceptable amendments or costs. | **Require documentary evidence of effective consent and fulfilled conditions before Completion**, waivable only by Buyer; approximately 30% of revenue is exposed. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Verified payout including interest/fees, discharge of all relevant security and guarantees, and correct debt-free/cash-free funds-flow treatment. | **Require repayment and effective releases at Completion through controlled payout arrangements**, with filing undertakings where needed; Buyer should not acquire unreleased secured debt. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional Completion bonuses described as Seller’s matter but omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller bears transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, without double counting adjustments. | **Verify triggers and on-costs, then expressly deduct/fund the liability and obtain a targeted indemnity**; omission could leave Buyer funding Seller’s transaction costs. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open, with no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Proven payment and enforceable ownership of relevant materials, plus protection against title defects, third-party claims and remediation costs. | **Require payment evidence and confirmatory assignment before Completion, backed by a broader specific indemnity**; paying an invoice alone may not secure usable IP rights. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary, not expected material; possible export of approximately **1,240 records**, with access, scope and notification duties unresolved. | Prompt investigation, preserved evidence, legal assessment of notification obligations, appropriate remediation and protection against pre-Completion incident liabilities. | **Require investigation milestones, disclosure updates and a specific indemnity; consider a holdback pending findings**; uncertainty warrants protection without assuming a confirmed breach or quantified loss. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals, **AUD 330,000 aggregate**, characterised as ordinary-course costs. | Assessment together of timing, scope, cancellation rights, accruals, commercial benefit and any departure from ordinary course. | **Review DD-008/DD-011 jointly and allocate under the agreed adjustment rules; require approval for new commitments**; neither ordinary-course status nor debt-like treatment is established. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply across all Claims unless expressly excluded. | Distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamentals, tax, specific indemnities, price/debt adjustments and fraud. | **Insert an express category/carve-out matrix with clear precedence**, preserving enforcement of completion and payment obligations; catch-all wording could neutralise negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register identifying Seller as holder of 100% of issued shares. | Independent verification of issued capital, ownership chain, encumbrances, options/conversion rights and transfer restrictions, plus valid transfer deliverables. | **Reconcile the register with corporate records and supporting documents, conduct relevant searches and obtain releases**; the register alone does not establish clean, transferable ownership. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties deemed settled under the general regime. | A separate pre-Completion tax covenant/indemnity with appropriate statutory-period survival, and robust IP ownership, licensing and infringement protection. | **Keep both open: negotiate bespoke tax protection and risk-based IP caps/survival, preserving the separate Ironquay indemnity**; neither risk is adequately addressed merely by general warranty treatment. |

**Completion priorities:** Bluefen’s effective consent and conditions, Riverlark repayment/releases, clean share title, and satisfactory resolution of Ironquay ownership. The bonus allocation and privacy investigation also require express contractual treatment—not reliance on disclosure alone.
=== END ADVICE ===
